title: Scope decision: planet moons (SE_PLMOON, sat/*.se1) and Body::Comet — port, descope, or remove the enum variants
description:
Gap found during the swisseph-rs/15 planning sweep (same class as the asteroid gap): `Body::PlanetMoon(PlanetMoonId)` and `Body::Comet(CometId)` exist in types.rs (lines 106–127) but have NO dispatch anywhere in calc — they fall through to the error path. Nobody planned the port.

Facts for the decision:
- C supports planetary moons since SE 2.10 via ipl = SE_PLMOON_OFFSET (9000) + encoded id, reading `sat/sepm*.se1` files. `../swisseph/ephe/sat/` EXISTS in the vendored checkout, so golden data generation is feasible.
- Implementation would closely follow the asteroid pattern from swisseph-rs/100–101 (SwissEphFile reader + provider wrapper + filename resolution) — estimated 1–2 Sonnet sub-tasks if we do it.
- Comets: in C 2.10.03 there is no real comet backend behind SE_COMET_OFFSET for swe_calc (comet-like bodies come through fictitious elements in seorbel.txt instead). Our `Body::Comet` variant is speculative API surface with nothing behind it.

Options:
1. Port planet moons (1–2 sub-tasks, needs a c-ref doc first) + remove `Body::Comet` until something real backs it.
2. Descope both for 1.0: keep variants, return a documented clean error (cheapest; variants already error today, just make the README/not-ported list say so — Polish 5/7 covers the README line either way).
3. Remove both variants from `Body` pre-1.0 (smallest honest API; can re-add without breakage later since adding enum variants is semver-minor with #[non_exhaustive]).

Recommendation: option 1 for planet moons if the Dart consumer will want them (lunar/planetary-moon work is niche but SE 2.10-parity is a clean marketing line); otherwise option 3 — shipping dead enum variants in a 1.0 API is the worst of the three. Decide, then this task becomes either a plan task (spawn c-ref-plmoon.md + implementation sub-task) or a small cleanup task.

decisions.decision: Option 1: full planetary-moon port (SE_PLMOON + SEFLG_CENTER_BODY) and removal of Body::Comet/CometId pre-1.0
decisions.rationale: SE 2.10 parity for the Dart consumer; repo ephe/sat/ already vendors all 32 sepm files so golden data is free; sweph_file parser already handles FileType::PlanetaryMoon incl. the exact rmax condition, so the remaining work is loading + dispatch. Comet has nothing behind it in C 2.10.03 (comet-like bodies go through seorbel.txt fictitious elements) — shipping a dead 1.0 enum variant is the worst option.
decisions.rejected_alternatives: Option 2 (keep both variants, documented clean error) — dead API surface in 1.0; Option 3 (remove both variants) — planet moons are real C 2.10 functionality with vendored data, removing them forfeits parity cheaply within reach.

decisions.decision: Port scoped as 3 tasks (125 loading -> 126 dispatch+goldens -> 127 MOSEPH/quirks/error coverage) + 1 independent removal task (128), mirroring the asteroid 100/101/102 split
decisions.rationale: The ref doc (docs/c-ref-plmoon.md, commit b80e37f) shows plmoon is NOT 'asteroid with a different directory': files hold planetocentric rectangular offsets (SEI_FLG_ROTATE clear, no sun-vector add) added onto the parent planet's barycentric position, and CENTER_BODY-on-planet vs direct 9pmm ipl are one normalization (sweph.c:416-437). So dispatch needs a new PlanetMoonProvider, and CENTER_BODY belongs in the same task as the body dispatch, not a separate one.
decisions.rejected_alternatives: Single mega-task (too large for one agent pass, loses the asteroid arc's proven review cadence); separate CENTER_BODY task (it is literally the same front-door translation — splitting would force both tasks to touch the same normalization code).

execution_record: Decision made (option 1) + planning executed in one session. Produced docs/c-ref-plmoon.md via a dedicated Sonnet C-reading agent (commit b80e37f) — key finding that reshaped the plan: plmoon .se1 files are planetocentric offset vectors (ROTATE clear, xsunb=NULL at both C call sites), combined by vector addition with the parent planet's independently-computed barycentric position, so the port is a new PlanetMoonProvider, not a re-parameterized AsteroidProvider. Also surfaced: single-step filename retry (not the asteroid 4-attempt cascade); rmax fine-scale is COB-or-Mars-moons only (already correctly implemented in parse.rs:329); the C-side H/G garbage-parse bug on plmoon file opens (do not port); nod_aps hard-rejects plmoon while get_orbital_elements silently degenerates (kept as C parity). Created swisseph-rs/125 (loading), 126 (dispatch + CENTER_BODY + SWIEPH/JPL goldens), 127 (MOSEPH/quirks/error paths/cross-function), 128 (Comet removal); 126 depends_on 125, 127 depends_on 126, 128 independent.
